slack.reconnect: Reconnect verifies or replaces credentials for this same Slack app. It does not reinstall the app or change its workspace or channel membership.
slack.remove: {{brand}} archives the endpoint, stops new ingress, and retires its saved Slack credentials. It does not uninstall the Slack app: the app remains installed, and its bot remains in channels, until you remove them in Slack.

github.reconnect: Reconnect verifies this same App and installation, then updates its webhook URL, secret, and secure delivery settings. It does not reinstall the App or change repository access.
github.remove: {{brand}} archives the endpoint, stops new ingress, and retires its saved App key and webhook secret. It does not uninstall the GitHub App: the App, its installations, and its webhook settings remain until you remove or update them on GitHub.

discord.reconnect: Reconnect verifies this same Discord application and server installation. It does not add or remove the bot from the server.
discord.remove: {{brand}} archives the endpoint, stops its {{brand}} Gateway connection, and retires its saved bot token. It does not uninstall the bot: the bot remains in the Discord server, and the application remains in the Developer Portal, until you remove them there.

microsoft-teams.reconnect: Reconnect verifies this same Microsoft app, tenant, and bot identity. It does not upload or reinstall the Teams app.
microsoft-teams.remove: {{brand}} archives the endpoint, stops new ingress, and retires its saved client secret. It does not uninstall the Teams app: the Entra app registration, Azure Bot, custom Teams app, and Teams installations remain until you remove them in Microsoft.

imessage-photon.reconnect: Reconnect verifies the same Photon project and line allocation, then recovers eligible missed messages.
imessage-photon.remove: Disconnect archives this channel and removes its saved secret. Your Photon project, number, subscription, and Messages history remain in Photon.

telegram.reconnect: Reconnect verifies this same BotFather bot and automatically refreshes its {{brand}} webhook and command menu.
telegram.remove: {{brand}} archives the endpoint and queues durable removal of its Telegram webhook and command menu. After Telegram confirms that cleanup, {{brand}} retires the saved token. The BotFather bot and its chat memberships remain until you remove them in Telegram.

worktree.title: Run tasks in this worktree
worktree.description: This is an isolated git-worktree preview instance. Turn this on to let the scheduler execute runs here. Only tasks created after enabling will run automatically — copied/pre-existing tasks stay parked. Toggling off and on resets the cutoff.
worktree.mismatchReason: This setting was armed in a different instance and copied here, so no tasks run automatically.
worktree.missingCutoffReason: This setting is missing its activation cutoff, so no tasks run automatically.
worktree.armHint: Toggle it off and back on to arm execution for tasks created here.

agentChat.title: Agent Chat
agentChat.description: Talk to each agent in one ongoing conversation. Clarify goals and create tasks for execution. Chat leads the Work group and opens an agent rail beside the nav, and each chat's side panel shows the agent's tasks and artifacts as cards.
agentChat.footnote: Turning this off preserves conversations and lets active runs finish, but prevents new messages.

artifactsV1.title: Artifacts V1
artifactsV1.description: Show artifacts the way the artifact directions lab settled: paper stacks and tiles on the Artifacts page, compact rows in the panel's Artifacts tab, and grouped rows in the task thread.
artifactsV1.footnote: Presentation only. Turning this off restores the current cards; no data changes.

betaSkills.title: Beta skills
betaSkills.description: Allow agents to pin beta releases of the {{brand}} core skill. Disabling this returns every agent to the default live skill without removing saved pins.

builtInAgents.title: Built-in Agents
builtInAgents.description: Show {{brand}}-managed built-in agent surfaces, including built-in roster badges, the Built-in agents tab, and built-in agent setup controls.

cases.title: Cases
cases.description: Durable work products (blog posts, tweet storms…) that tasks create and iterate on. Adds the Cases tab and the agent case API.
cases.footnote: Turning Cases off hides the tab and blocks the case API; existing case data is kept.

chatConnectors.title: Chat connectors
chatConnectors.description: Connect agents to Slack, Discord, Microsoft Teams, and Telegram conversations.
chatConnectors.footnote: Turning this off hides experimental chat setup and connected-task controls. Existing chat connections keep running. AgentMail, GitHub review bots, and tool connectors are controlled separately.

combinedInbox.title: Combined Inbox + Task List
combinedInbox.description: Fold Inbox into Tasks. One Tasks row carries the unread badge, and a Views menu reaches every inbox view (Mine, Unread, Blocked, Recent, Everything) and every task view.
combinedInbox.footnote: Old Inbox links redirect to the matching view. Turning this off restores the separate Inbox; no data changes.
combinedInbox.ariaLabel: Toggle combined inbox and task list experimental setting

conferenceRoom.title: Conference Room Chat
conferenceRoom.description: Adds a Conference Room — one chat where you and your whole team work together — plus the live activity feed and the redesigned onboarding. Also restyles task threads as chat bubbles. Turn off anytime to restore the classic UI.
conferenceRoom.ariaLabel: Toggle conference room chat experimental setting

decisions.title: Decisions
decisions.description: Show the Decisions item in the main sidebar — the attention home that surfaces the tasks awaiting your input — while the surface is still being evaluated.

environments.title: Enable Environments
environments.description: Show environment management in company settings and allow project and agent environment assignment controls.

externalObjects.title: Enable External Objects
externalObjects.description: Detect external URLs in issues and show resolved status for pull requests, tickets, and other referenced work objects.

isolatedWorkspaces.title: Enable Isolated Workspaces
isolatedWorkspaces.description: Show execution workspace controls in project configuration and allow isolated workspace behavior for new and existing task runs.

fastResponses.title: Experimental fast responses
fastResponses.description: Allow short acknowledgements while agents begin work. Configure them in Settings → Connections.

fileViewer.title: Experimental File Viewer
fileViewer.description: Show task detail controls for browsing and previewing workspace files relative to a task.

firstTaskPlan.title: First task: propose with a plan document
firstTaskPlan.description: When the user's first request is a single task, the chief of staff writes a short plan document and a checkbox card instead of a one-card confirmation. Applies to organizations created after the toggle is flipped.
firstTaskPlan.ariaLabel: Toggle first task plan proposal experimental setting

githubReviewBots.title: GitHub review bots
githubReviewBots.description: Connect agents to GitHub with their own App identity to review pull requests and respond to issues.
githubReviewBots.footnote: Independent of Chat connectors. Turning this off hides setup and management; existing bots keep running. GitHub tool connections stay available.
githubReviewBots.ariaLabel: Toggle GitHub review bots experimental setting

grokBot.title: Grok Bot
grokBot.description: Connect an existing Grok Bot as an agent. Verify routine delivery and an authenticated reply before assigning work.
grokBot.footnote: Requires {{brand}} Runner and authenticated public HTTPS. Usage is not reported. Turning this off blocks Grok calls and new dispatch.

memoryConnectors.title: Memory connectors
memoryConnectors.description: Connect Mem0, Zep, Supermemory, Cognee, and Honcho for long-term memory and context.
memoryConnectors.footnote: Turning this off hides setup for these connectors. Existing connections keep running.

muse.title: Muse — Personal agent
muse.description: Connect your personal Meta Muse. Pair it, detect its receiver, and verify an independent background reply before assigning tasks.
muse.footnote: Requires {{brand}} Runner and an authenticated instance with a public HTTPS URL. Turning this off blocks new work; cleanup and stop evidence remain available. Provider usage and cost are unavailable.

openAiDot.title: OpenAI Dot
openAiDot.description: Add OpenAI Dot as a standalone agent choice. Pair your Dot and verify event delivery before assigning work.
openAiDot.footnote: Requires an authenticated instance with a public HTTPS URL. Turning this off blocks Dot calls and new work; saved connections are kept.

paperclipRunner.title: {{brand}} Runner
paperclipRunner.description: Allow agents to select {{brand}} Runner, including authenticated runner ingress when a sandbox requires it. First-run setup offers qualified GitHub Copilot. Turning this off hides the choice without affecting existing native runs.

simplifiedEnglish.title: Simplified English Interactions
simplifiedEnglish.description: Instruct agents to write user interactions (plan confirmations, questions, suggested tasks, checkbox prompts) in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English, with brief context on what information the decision needs and what happens for each choice.
simplifiedEnglish.ariaLabel: Toggle simplified english interactions experimental setting

statusCards.title: Status Cards
statusCards.description: Enable the experimental shared status-card board and its gated API. Existing card data is kept when this is disabled.
statusCards.footnote: Enabling Status Cards also enables Summaries.

streamlinedUi.title: Streamlined UI
streamlinedUi.description: Use the simplified main sidebar, shared Tasks and Inbox presentation, focused task detail layout, and contextual navigation across Agents, Routines, Skills, and Settings.
streamlinedUi.footnote: Turning this off restores the legacy shell and navigation. Task and page data are unchanged.

summaries.title: Summaries
summaries.description: Show Summarizer-generated status slots on project and workspace pages, with on-demand refresh and revision history. Existing summary data is kept when this is disabled.
summaries.footnote: Status Cards requires Summaries. Disabling Summaries also disables Status Cards.

isolatedWorkspacesDefault.title: Use Isolated Workspaces By Default
isolatedWorkspacesDefault.description: Treat a project that has no execution workspace policy of its own as if it selected isolated workspaces, so its tasks get a per-task worktree instead of sharing the project checkout. A project that carries its own policy keeps it.
isolatedWorkspacesDefault.ariaLabel: Toggle isolated workspaces by default experimental setting

devAutoRestart.title: Auto-Restart Dev Server When Idle
devAutoRestart.description: In `pnpm dev:once`, wait for all queued and running local agent runs to finish, then restart the server automatically when backend changes or migrations make the current boot stale.

devManagedSandboxOnly.title: Managed Environment Only
devManagedSandboxOnly.description: Hide the local environment and run all agents in the platform-managed environment.
devManagedSandboxOnly.ariaLabel: Toggle managed environment only experimental setting

devDeveloperMode.title: {{brand}} Developer Mode
devDeveloperMode.description: Show internal {{brand}} maintainer tools and observability links, including Honeycomb trace queries on run pages.

devServerInfo.title: Server Info Debug View
devServerInfo.description: Show a "Server" section in the account drawer with the current server restart time and running commit.
devServerInfo.ariaLabel: Toggle server info debug view experimental setting

devSmokeLab.title: Smoke Lab
devSmokeLab.description: Add a "Smoke Lab" tab under Apps → Developer and an "Integration smoke" card on the dashboard for exercising every integration path against deterministic local fixtures (fake OAuth provider + loopback MCP servers). Private (non-public) deployments only.

devTaskPlanDecomposition.title: Task Plan Decomposition
devTaskPlanDecomposition.description: Show accepted-plan decomposition history on task detail pages. Intended for debugging and validating subtask creation behavior while the presentation is still being refined.
devTaskPlanDecomposition.ariaLabel: Toggle task plan decomposition panel experimental setting

classicTaskInterface.title: Classic Task Interface
classicTaskInterface.description: Restores the previous task detail page: the page-level header with inline description editing, the plain comment thread, and the fixed Properties sidebar. Chat-only features — streaming activity folding, inline plan and question cards, the three-mode composer — are unavailable in the classic view.
classicTaskInterface.footnote: Switching takes effect immediately. No task data is affected.
classicTaskInterface.ariaLabel: Toggle classic task interface experimental setting

goalsSidebarLink.title: Goals Sidebar Link
goalsSidebarLink.description: Restore the Goals item in the main sidebar while the goals surface is being evaluated.
goalsSidebarLink.ariaLabel: Toggle goals sidebar link experimental setting

mcpTasks.title: Durable app actions (MCP Tasks)
mcpTasks.description: Let connected apps run long actions, such as CI runs or deploys, as tasks {{brand}} keeps track of. If an action outlasts a call, a restart, or a deploy, the agent collects the result later and the work is never started twice.
mcpTasks.footnote: Applies to apps that support MCP Tasks. Turning this off stops new tasks; apps then answer as before.
mcpTasks.ariaLabel: Toggle durable app actions experimental setting

legacyComposer.title: Command/Ctrl+Enter to Submit
legacyComposer.description: Restore the previous keyboard shortcut for task replies and new tasks: Command/Ctrl+Enter submits, and Enter adds a new line.
legacyComposer.footnote: Off by default: Enter submits, and Shift+Enter adds a new line.

googleWorkspace.title: Google Workspace connector ({{brand}})
googleWorkspace.description: Show the built-in Google Workspace connector for Gmail, Drive, and Calendar while Google verification is pending.
googleWorkspace.footnote: Off by default. While off, Google apps are offered through Composio and Arcade instead, and the built-in connector cannot be set up or run.
googleWorkspace.ariaLabel: Toggle {{brand}} Google Workspace connector experimental setting

responsibilities.title: Areas & Responsibilities dashboard
responsibilities.description: Replace the classic dashboard with one built around the areas you care about and the responsibilities you own in each. An agent can interview you to create it, and you can undo any change.
responsibilities.footnote: Turning this off brings back the classic dashboard. Your areas and responsibilities are kept.
responsibilities.ariaLabel: Toggle Areas & Responsibilities dashboard experimental setting

awsConnector.title: AWS connector
awsConnector.description: Let agents work in AWS through AWS's hosted MCP server, with short-lived credentials made for each connection.
awsConnector.footnote: Off by default. While off, the AWS connector cannot be set up or run.

teams.title: Connect {{agent}} to Microsoft Teams
teams.repairing: Reconnect verifies this same Microsoft app, tenant, and bot identity. It does not upload or reinstall the Teams app. Leave fields blank to reuse saved credentials.
teams.intro: Use your own Microsoft app credentials for this bot.
teams.requirements: This setup requires a Microsoft 365 work or school organization where you can register an Entra app, create an Azure Bot, and upload or install a Teams app. Personal or free Teams accounts at teams.live.com cannot complete this setup. This release supports Microsoft 365 commercial cloud tenants only; GCC, GCC High, DoD, and Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet are not supported yet.
teams.stepEntra: In Microsoft Entra, create a single-tenant app registration. Copy its Application (client) ID and Directory (tenant) ID, then create a client secret and copy its value.
teams.stepAzureBot: In Azure, create an Azure Bot. Choose Single Tenant, use that Application ID, set its messaging endpoint to the {{brand}} URL below, and add the Microsoft Teams channel.
teams.stepTeamsApp: In Teams Developer Portal, create an app, add a bot with the same Application ID, then apply the manifest settings shown below. The block binds the Teams resource-specific consent permissions to that Entra app; these are not Microsoft Graph permissions in Entra. These permissions let the installed app receive every message in a team or group chat without an @mention, so describe that access to installers. Download the package and install it in the target team or group chat.

pathInstructionsModal.title: How to get a full path

mac.step1: Open Finder and navigate to the folder.
mac.step3: Hold the Option (⌥) key — "Copy" changes to "Copy as Pathname".
mac.step4: Click "Copy as Pathname", then paste here.
mac.tip: You can also open Terminal, type cd, drag the folder into the terminal window, and press Enter. Then type pwd to see the full path.

windows.step1: Open File Explorer and navigate to the folder.
windows.step2: Click in the address bar at the top — the full path will appear.
windows.step3: Copy the path, then paste here.
windows.tip: Alternatively, hold Shift and right-click the folder, then select "Copy as path".

linux.step1: Open a terminal and navigate to the directory with cd.
linux.step2: Run pwd to print the full path.
linux.step3: Copy the output and paste here.
linux.tip: In most file managers, Ctrl+L reveals the full path in the address bar.

agentConfigHelp.dangerouslySkipPermissions: Run unattended by auto-approving adapter permission prompts when supported.
agentConfigHelp.dangerouslyBypassSandbox: Run Codex without sandbox restrictions. Required for filesystem/network access.
agentConfigHelp.search: Enable Codex web search capability during runs.
agentConfigHelp.fastMode: Enable Codex Fast mode. This burns credits/tokens much faster and is supported on GPT-6, GPT-5.6, GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4, and manual Codex model IDs.
agentConfigHelp.workspaceStrategy: How {{brand}} should realize an execution workspace for this agent. Keep project_primary for normal cwd execution, or use git_worktree for issue-scoped isolated checkouts.
agentConfigHelp.workspaceBaseRef: Base git ref used when creating a worktree branch. Leave blank to use the resolved workspace ref or HEAD.
agentConfigHelp.workspaceBranchTemplate: Template for naming derived branches. Supports {{issue.identifier}}, {{issue.title}}, {{agent.name}}, {{project.id}}, {{workspace.repoRef}}, and {{slug}}.
agentConfigHelp.worktreeParentDir: Directory where derived worktrees should be created. Absolute, ~-prefixed, and repo-relative paths are supported.
agentConfigHelp.runtimeServicesJson: Optional workspace runtime service definitions. Use this for shared app servers, workers, or other long-lived companion processes attached to the workspace.
agentConfigHelp.maxTurnsPerRun: Maximum number of agentic turns (tool calls) per heartbeat run.
agentConfigHelp.command: The command to execute (e.g. node, python).
agentConfigHelp.localCommand: Override the path to the CLI command you want the adapter to call (e.g. /usr/local/bin/claude, codex, opencode).
agentConfigHelp.extraArgs: Extra CLI arguments for local adapters, comma-separated.
agentConfigHelp.envVars: Environment variables injected into the adapter process. Use plain values or secret references.
agentConfigHelp.secretAccess: Secrets this agent can reach. Env-var bindings are injected at run start; API-access bindings are fetched on demand via the run-bound agent API and never written to the environment.
agentConfigHelp.bootstrapPrompt: Only sent when {{brand}} starts a fresh session. Use this for stable setup guidance that should not be repeated on every heartbeat.
agentConfigHelp.payloadTemplateJson: Optional JSON merged into remote adapter request payloads before {{brand}} adds its standard wake and workspace fields.
agentConfigHelp.webhookUrl: The URL that receives POST requests when the agent is invoked.
agentConfigHelp.heartbeatInterval: Run this agent automatically on a timer. Useful for periodic tasks like checking for new work.
agentConfigHelp.timeoutSec: Maximum seconds a run can take before being terminated. 0 means no timeout.
